page.title: Trust & Security — Smart Food Safe
page.description: How Smart Food Safe protects your data: certifications, security architecture, privacy, and reliability at a glance.

hero.title: Your food-safety operations, secured at every layer.
hero.description: Smart Food Safe is a secure, scalable SaaS platform built to protect business-critical data and keep global teams running with confidence. Enterprise-grade controls, independent assurance, and resilient cloud infrastructure are built into every layer.

pillars.title: Six ways we protect your data
pillars.description: Security isn't a single feature - it's designed into every layer of the platform. Here's how it holds together.

items.title: Certified & audited
items.description: ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II, with independent external audits and GDPR compliance built into how we operate.

items.title: Encrypted everywhere
items.description: AES-256 for data at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit. Passwords are stored hashed, never in plain text.

items.title: Access on least privilege
items.description: Role-based access, SSO with Microsoft and Google, and multi-factor authentication for every user.

items.title: Resilient by design
items.description: Auto-scaling AWS architecture with a replicated database, daily encrypted backups, and tested disaster recovery.

items.title: Your data stays yours
items.description: You own your data at all times, can export it on request, and it's never used for commercial purposes.

items.title: Watched around the clock
items.description: Continuous monitoring, full audit logging, and a proactive incident-response process with clear response times.

sections.title: Built on a resilient cloud foundation
sections.description: Smart Food Safe is a multi-tenant SaaS platform hosted on Amazon Web Services, engineered to scale and to stay available.
specs: Amazon Web Services (AWS), primary region eu-west-1 (Ireland). Fully cloud-based - no customer-deployed software required.
Containerized microservices on AWS ECS with blue/green deployments and auto-scaling; CloudFront and S3 for delivery and storage.
MongoDB Atlas replica set across multiple nodes, with compute and storage auto-scaling and cross-region backup snapshots.
Logical isolation per customer using a unique tenant identifier and row-level security.
Engineered for 99.9% uptime. Real-time status is published at status.smartfoodsafe.com.
Automated daily backups, encrypted in transit and at rest, with quarterly restoration testing.
Documented, tested DR runbook with cross-region failover. Most recent test recovered all mission-critical modules within target.
Continuous monitoring via AWS CloudWatch, Datadog, and Grafana, with real-time alerting and full audit logging.

faq.title: Security questions, answered clearly
faq.description: Details about our independent application testing, remediation practices, platform safeguards, data handling, and service resilience.

groups.title: Independent assessment & assurance
items: Has Smart Food Safe undergone penetration testing?
Yes. Scrut Automation conducted an independent web-application vulnerability assessment and penetration test using both manual and automated methods. The final report was issued on February 18, 2026.
What was included in the assessment?

The review covered the staging web application and included authenticated and unauthenticated testing, application fingerprinting, vulnerability scanning, manual analysis, safe exploitation where appropriate, and retesting. Testing was aligned with the OWASP Top 10 and covered areas such as authentication, authorization, sessions, input validation, cryptography, business logic, configuration, and client-side security.
Does a penetration test guarantee that no vulnerabilities exist?

No. A penetration test provides a point-in-time assessment of the tested environment and scope. New issues can emerge as applications, dependencies, and attack techniques change, so testing is part of an ongoing vulnerability-management program.
Can customers request the full report?

The detailed report contains confidential technical evidence and is shared with eligible customers and prospects through the appropriate review process. Contact our team to request security documentation.

groups.title: Findings & remediation
items: What did the 2026 assessment find?

The assessment reported five findings: one medium-severity issue and four low-severity issues. No critical or high-severity findings were reported. The findings related to API-key restrictions, third-party script controls, input validation, Content Security Policy, and outdated software components.
Were the findings remediated?

At the report's February 18, 2026 retest, the medium-severity API-key issue and two low-severity browser-security issues were marked fixed. Two low-severity items - server-side input validation and vulnerable component versions - remained open and were identified for remediation. Statuses here reflect that dated report and may change as remediation and validation continue.
How are vulnerabilities prioritized?

Findings are evaluated by severity, exploitability, and potential impact. Remediation focuses first on higher-risk issues, while lower-risk findings are tracked through the vulnerability-management process and retested to confirm that fixes are effective.
How does Smart Food Safe reduce injection and browser-based risks?

Controls include server-side input validation, secure-coding practices, dependency updates, restricted external resources, and Content Security Policy headers. These safeguards are supported by recurring scanning, manual testing, and remediation tracking.

groups.title: Platform protection & access
items: How is customer data encrypted?
Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and protected in transit using TLS 1.2 or later. Passwords are stored as hashes rather than plain text.
How is access to the platform controlled?
Smart Food Safe uses role-based access control and least-privilege principles. The platform supports single sign-on with Microsoft and Google, along with multi-factor authentication.
How is each customer's data separated?
Each customer is assigned a unique tenant identifier, with logical isolation and row-level security used to keep tenant data separated within the multi-tenant SaaS platform.
How is suspicious activity detected?

Infrastructure and application activity is continuously monitored with real-time alerting and audit logging. Monitoring includes AWS CloudWatch, Datadog, and Grafana, supported by an incident-response process.

groups.title: Privacy, continuity & recovery
items: Who owns customer data?
Customers retain ownership of their data. It is not used for commercial purposes and can be exported on request in standard formats such as CSV, JSON, Excel, and PDF.
What happens to data when a customer leaves?
Data can be exported and is then securely deleted in line with the applicable retention, disposal, and sanitization procedures.
How are backups and disaster recovery handled?

Automated daily backups are encrypted in transit and at rest, with restoration testing performed quarterly. A documented disaster-recovery runbook supports cross-region failover and recovery of mission-critical services.
What availability does Smart Food Safe target?
The platform is engineered for 99.9% uptime using auto-scaling cloud infrastructure, replicated data services, monitoring, backups, and tested recovery procedures.
